const prev = $input.item.json;

// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// stripBoilerplate v1: removes UI chrome that has zero job signal.
// Patterns target only chrome that cannot appear in legitimate posting
// content (cookie banners, skip-to-content, social/share, footer ©).
// Does NOT touch STRUCTURED DATA blocks or job text, pure regex on
// known-junk lines. Conservative on purpose.
// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
function stripBoilerplate(text) {
  if (!text || text.length < 200) return text || '';
  let out = String(text);
  const PATTERNS = [
    /^.*\b(?:we use cookies|cookie (?:settings|preferences|policy|notice|consent|banner)|accept (?:all )?cookies|manage cookies|cookies and (?:tracking|similar))\b.*$/gim,
    /^\s*skip to (?:main )?content.*$/gim,
    /^\s*skip navigation.*$/gim,
    /^\s*back to (?:top|search results|search|jobs|listings|results).*$/gim,
    /^\s*(?:view|see) all (?:jobs|positions|openings|opportunities)\s*$/gim,
    /^.*\bsubscribe to (?:our )?(?:newsletter|updates|alerts|emails)\b.*$/gim,
    /^.*\bsign up for (?:our )?(?:newsletter|alerts|updates|job alerts|emails)\b.*$/gim,
    /^\s*follow us on\b.*$/gim,
    /^\s*share (?:this )?(?:job|posting|opportunity|page|via)\b.*$/gim,
    /^\s*share on (?:facebook|twitter|linkedin|email|whatsapp)\b.*$/gim,
    /^\s*\u00a9\s*(?:19|20)\d{2}\b.*$/gim,
    /^\s*copyright\s*\u00a9?\s*(?:19|20)\d{2}\b.*$/gim,
    /^\s*all rights reserved\.?\s*$/gim,
  ];
  for (const p of PATTERNS) out = out.replace(p, '');
  // Collapse 3+ consecutive blank lines into 2
  out = out.replace(/\n[ \t]*\n[ \t]*\n+/g, '\n\n').trim();
  return out;
}

// Clean UI chrome from page text BEFORE sending to LLM (saves tokens, no content loss).
const cleanedPageText = stripBoilerplate(prev.page_text || '');

// ����── RULEBOOK (static: identical across all 1,601 calls/day then cacheable) ───
const RULEBOOK = `Extract job data. Return ONE JSON object. No prose, no markdown.

=====================
PRIMARY POSTING ONLY — READ THIS FIRST
=====================
This page may contain sidebar widgets, footer sections, or "Similar Jobs" / "Related Jobs" / "Other Positions" / "You May Also Like" / "More Jobs" / "Recommended Jobs" panels listing OTHER job postings. These are NOT part of the job you are processing.

RULE: Extract data ONLY from the main job posting at the top of the content. Ignore EVERYTHING that appears to be a listing of other jobs. Specifically:
• Any block that shows multiple job titles + locations in rapid succession is a "similar jobs" widget — ignore it entirely.
• Location, salary, role_name, role_desc, and role_qual must come ONLY from the primary posting, not from other jobs listed on the same page.
• If you are unsure whether a location belongs to THIS job or to a similar-jobs widget, use only the HIRING LOCATIONS from the STRUCTURED DATA section below.
• The "=== STRUCTURED DATA (authoritative) ===" section at the top of the POSTING is machine-extracted from THIS specific job's schema — it is always about this job only. Trust it over page text when they conflict.
=====================

IMPORTANT — STRUCTURED DATA:
=====================
If the posting text begins with "=== STRUCTURED DATA (authoritative) ===", that section contains machine-extracted data from the page's JSON-LD schema. It is MORE RELIABLE than the rest of the text. Specifically:
• "HIRING LOCATIONS:" lists the actual job site addresses (with full street address when available). Use the COMPLETE address string as-is — do NOT abbreviate to just "City, State" when a full street address is given. These are the definitive locations; ignore any conflicting page text mentions.
• "JOB DESCRIPTION (from structured data):" contains the full job description including salary/compensation — read it carefully for pay information.
• "STRUCTURED SALARY:" if present, is the salary from structured data — always use it.
• "STRUCTURED ROLE TITLE:" if present, use it as role_name even if the description mentions another role name.
• "STRUCTURED JOB TYPE:" if present, use it as job_type. Do not infer full-time from benefits sections.

=====================
SCHEMA:
{
  "role_name": string,
  "role_desc": string,
  "role_qual": string,
  "address": string|null,
  "multiple_locations": "yes"|"no",
  "location_skip_reason": null|"non_us"|"all_not_allowed",
  "workplace_type": "Onsite"|"Remote"|"Hybrid",
  "pay_min": number|null,
  "pay_max": number|null,
  "minimum_year": number,
  "minimum_year_source": "stated"|"inferred",
  "job_type": "full-time"|"part-time"|"internship",
  "also_part_time": "yes"|"no",
  "seasonal": "yes"|"no",
  "pay_unit": "hourly"|"salary"|"invalid",
  "skip_reason": null|"no_salary"|"no_address"|"invalid_pay_unit"|"all_not_allowed"|"non_us"
}

ALLOWED STATES (the only 10 US states): CA, CT, IL, DC, NJ, NY, RI, VA, MD, WA.
Every other US state (MT, CO, AZ, TX, FL, GA, NC, OH, PA, MA, WI, MN, MI, IN, MO, TN, AL, OK, NV, OR, UT, KS, NE, IA, AR, KY, LA, MS, SC, WV, AK, HI, ID, WY, SD, ND, VT, NH, ME, DE) is NOT allowed.

=====================
NON-US CHECK — DO THIS FIRST, BEFORE ANYTHING
=====================
Only mark non_us if there are ZERO allowed US hiring locations.

IMPORTANT EXCEPTION: If the posting lists BOTH non-US locations AND allowed US locations, IGNORE the non-US locations completely and process only the allowed US hiring locations. Do NOT set non_us in this case.

Only return:
  address = null
  location_skip_reason = "non_us"
  skip_reason = "non_us"
...when there are absolutely no allowed US hiring locations at all.

Any country outside the United States is non_us — use your knowledge of world geography to identify them (e.g., Mexico, Canada, UK, Philippines, India, Germany, Australia, etc.). US territories — Puerto Rico, Guam, US Virgin Islands, American Samoa, Northern Mariana Islands — are ALSO treated as non_us for filtering purposes.

"all_not_allowed" is ONLY for postings where every hiring location is a US state NOT in the 10 allowed. "all_not_allowed" does NOT apply to foreign countries. If a posting has both non-US locations AND allowed US locations, use PATH 3b — ignore the non-US locations, process only the allowed US ones.

=====================
LOCATION EXTRACTION (for US-only postings)
=====================

Step A — HIRING LOCATIONS ONLY. Identify actual hiring locations. These usually appear:
- in the posting header or title ("City, State | City, State | ...")
- in a "Location:" field
- in a tagline near the top ("Full Time • 19th Street")
- in a "This position is based out of..." sentence
- in URL slugs for single-location postings

Do NOT count as hiring locations:
- Operational scope phrases ("manages 4-6 shops", "oversees 10 stores", "portfolio of regions")
- Travel territory ("travel throughout the region", "across the United States", "Rocky Mountain region")
- Office counts ("13 locations", "offices nationwide", "550 offices")
- Region mentions ("the region", "the western United States", "nationwide")
- Corporate/HQ/mailing addresses

Step B — Build an internal list of ACTUAL hiring cities/states.
Step C — For each, classify Allowed (one of the 10) or Not-Allowed.
Step D — Choose the path:

PATH 1: ALL hiring locations are outside the US AND there are zero allowed US hiring locations → non_us. Stop. (If there is even one allowed US location, use PATH 3b instead — do NOT set non_us.)

PATH 2: Every US hiring location is in NON-allowed US states → address=null, location_skip_reason="all_not_allowed", skip_reason="all_not_allowed".
  Example: Billings MT, Helena MT, Missoula MT, Lakewood CO, Phoenix AZ → every state non-allowed → all_not_allowed.
  Example: only Texas and Florida → all_not_allowed.

PATH 3: Mixed US states — some allowed, some not allowed. // path3-fix-v5
Count only the ALLOWED state locations (ignore non-allowed ones).
  • If exactly 1 allowed location → treat exactly like PATH 4: use the full address from HIRING LOCATIONS
    (street + city + state + zip if available), multiple_locations="no".
  • If 2 or more allowed locations → address = count of allowed locations as a plain number string
    (e.g. "2"), multiple_locations="yes".
  • If 0 allowed locations and all are non-US → use PATH 1 (non_us) instead.
  • "all_not_allowed" is ONLY for 0 allowed AND all locations are US states not in the 10 allowed.

PATH 3b: Non-US + allowed US locations present → ignore non-US entirely, process only the allowed US locations as PATH 4 or 5. Do NOT set non_us.
  Example: Los Angeles CA + Toronto Canada → ignore Toronto → address="Los Angeles, CA", multiple_locations="no".

PATH 4: Single US hiring location in allowed state → use the FULL address exactly as listed in HIRING LOCATIONS (e.g. "555 South Flower Street, Los Angeles, California, 90071"). If only City/State is available, use "City, State". Append " - Facility Name" if a specific facility/branch/office/clinic/center is named in the posting or URL slug. multiple_locations="no".
  Example: URL "careers.example-healthcare.com/job/westminster/..." + "Westminster Surgery Center" → "Westminster, Maryland - Westminster Surgery Center".
  Example: HIRING LOCATIONS shows "555 South Flower Street, Los Angeles, California, 90071, United States" → address="555 South Flower Street, Los Angeles, California, 90071".

PATH 5: Multiple US hiring locations, EVERY location in allowed states → address = count as string, multiple_locations="yes". (Downstream: Qualified.)
  Example: Pasadena CA, San Francisco CA, San Diego CA, Long Beach CA → "4" (all CA, all allowed).

PATH 6: Zero hiring addresses → address=null, skip_reason="no_address".

LOCATION RESCUE RULE: If HIRING LOCATIONS is ambiguous or lists only non-allowed states, scan the full job description body for any mention of the 10 allowed states (CA/California, CT/Connecticut, IL/Illinois, DC/District of Columbia, NJ/New Jersey, NY/New York, RI/Rhode Island, VA/Virginia, MD/Maryland, WA/Washington). If found, use PATH 3/4/5 logic with those states. Disregard mentions in navigation links, "similar jobs" widgets, or page footer — focus only on the actual job description text.

SINGLE-LOCATION SANITY CHECK:
If only ONE hiring location is named (e.g. "19th Street", one city, one shop name), set multiple_locations="no" — even if the posting describes the role as overseeing multiple shops/regions. Do NOT mark multi-location based on role scope. Location count is about hiring sites, not managed sites.

=====================
MIN YEAR
=====================
- Stated number → use it.
- Range "7-10 yrs" → min (7).
- "Relevant experience" no number → 1.
- Not mentioned → infer: Intern=0, Junior=1, Mid=3, Senior=5, Lead=7, Director=10.
- AGE IS NOT EXPERIENCE (MANDATORY): "must be at least 18 years old", "must be 18 years of age or older", "21 years of age", "minimum age 21", "under the age of 18" are LEGAL/LICENSING age requirements. They are NOT years of experience. NEVER copy 16/18/21 (or any age) into minimum_year. If the posting states an age but no experience, infer minimum_year from the role level instead.
- COMPANY TENURE IS NOT EXPERIENCE: "a company with more than 36 years of experience", "serving clients for 40 years" describes the EMPLOYER, not the candidate. Never use those numbers.
- minimum_year is realistically 0-15. A larger number almost always means you picked up an age or a company age — re-read and use the candidate requirement.

=====================
ROLE DESC (HARD RULES — formatting is the whole point of this automation)
=====================
HARD RULE 1 (MANDATORY, non-negotiable): role_desc MUST begin with the literal word "Description" on its own line, followed by a blank line. This header is ALWAYS added — even when the source posting has no header, has a different header ("Summary", "Overview", "About the Role", "The Role:"), or opens with a hook sentence. Never skip. Never rename. Never move. "Description" is line 1, always.

- Do NOT include any sentences or paragraphs about the company, its history, mission, values, "For over N years...", "Who We Are", "About Us", or similar filler.
- Do NOT include any links (http/https), URLs, or references to external websites.
- Do NOT include any emojis, emoticons, or decorative symbols (★, ✓, etc.).

HARD RULE 2 (ROLE_DESC = FULL POSTING, ROLE_QUAL = SUBSET): // role-desc-qual-fix-v5
role_desc must contain EVERYTHING in the job posting that describes the role — the full narrative
from top to bottom: what the job is, what you will do, AND all qualification/requirement sections.
role_qual is a subset extracted from role_desc. The golden rule: if content is not in role_desc, it
MUST NOT appear in role_qual. Qualifications always go at the BOTTOM of role_desc.

Concretely: after writing the main job narrative in role_desc, append all qualification/requirement
sections verbatim at the bottom of role_desc (labeled with their original section headings on their
own lines). Then ALSO copy that qualification content into role_qual in the organized format.

NEVER put content in role_qual that is absent from role_desc. role_desc is the master record.

HARD RULE 3: preserve source wording and source headings. Do NOT rephrase/shorten/rename existing section titles. If source says "PRIMARY JOB RESPONSIBILITIES", keep it. If source says "A Day in the Life", keep it. Only clean obvious typos or messy whitespace.

HARD RULE 4: do NOT duplicate headers. Responsibilities-family headings (Responsibilities / Primary Job Responsibilities / Duties / Key Responsibilities / A Day in the Life / Key Job Responsibilities) �� pick the one the source used, do not add a second one. Same for Requirements/Qualifications-family (Requirements / Qualifications / JOB SPECIFICATIONS / Required Knowledge-Skills-Attributes / Education / Experience-Qualifications / Experience/Qualifications) — keep what the source used.

HARD RULE 5 (BENEFITS — EXCLUDE COMPLETELY): Do NOT include benefits, perks, or compensation extras in role_desc at all. Skip any content under headings like "Benefits", "WHAT WE OFFER", "Why Choose Us", "Perks", "Our Benefits Include", "Life at [Company]", "The perks of working at ... include", "Our Offer", "Compensation & Benefits", "Total Rewards". This includes: health/dental/vision insurance, 401k/retirement, PTO/vacation/sick leave, parental leave, tuition reimbursement, employee discounts, wellness programs, gym memberships, free meals, commuter benefits, life insurance, disability insurance, EAP, stock options, RSUs, bonuses (referenced as benefit), and similar. Only the actual pay/salary stays — and that goes into pay_min/pay_max fields, not role_desc.

HARD RULE 7 (ANTI-RUN-ON, MANDATORY): NEVER output role_desc as one run-on paragraph. Each responsibility, requirement, qualification, skill, education item, certification, or schedule bullet MUST be on its own line prefixed with "• ".
  - If the source lists items on separate lines (even without bullet characters like "*" or "-"), each line IS a list item — output each as its own "• " line.
  - Example source (no bullet chars, just newlines):
      Consults with and keeps supervisor informed...
      Provides general nursing care such as...
      Takes and records temperature...
    MUST become:
      • Consults with and keeps supervisor informed...
      • Provides general nursing care such as...
      • Takes and records temperature...
  - NEVER concatenate list items into a single paragraph. NEVER separate items with only periods.
  - Section headings (Essential Functions, Responsibilities, Qualifications, Knowledge/Skills/Abilities, Education, Licenses/Certification, Experience) live on their own line with a blank line before and after.

HARD RULE 8: output MUST include \n (newline) characters liberally. Between every list item. Between every section. Between header and body. If you return a paragraph with no newlines, the result is WRONG.

HARD RULE 9 (HEADING SEPARATION — MANDATORY): ANY heading written in ALL-CAPS or ending with "?" (e.g. "WHAT IS THE OPPORTUNITY?", "WHAT WILL YOU DO?", "WHAT DO YOU NEED TO SUCCEED?", "WHAT'S IN IT FOR YOU?", "WHAT WILL YOU DO?") MUST be on its own line with a blank line BEFORE and AFTER it. Never write "WHAT IS THE OPPORTUNITY?Responsible for..." — always write "WHAT IS THE OPPORTUNITY?\n\nResponsible for...". This applies to EVERY all-caps or question-format heading in the source.

HARD RULE 10 (PLAIN TEXT ONLY — NO MARKDOWN): role_name, role_desc and role_qual must be PLAIN TEXT. Never emit markdown syntax, even when the source posting uses it. Specifically: no "#"/"##"/"###" heading marks, no "**bold**" or "__bold__", no "*italic*" or "_italic_", no backticks, no "[text](url)" links, no "![image](url)", no "---"/"***" rules, no "|" tables. Write a heading as its own plain line ("Additional Information", never "### Additional Information"). Write emphasis as ordinary words ("Job Type: Full-time", never "**Job Type:** Full-time"). Bullets are "• " only.

HARD RULE 6 — EXCLUDE completely: About Us / Who We Are / Who Are We / company history / mission / values / "For over N years..." / "Leading with Science" / URLs / emojis / EEO statements ("Equal Opportunity Employer", "M/F Disabled and Vet") / application instructions / req IDs / awards / taglines / "Your Impact" / "Why [Company]" filler paragraphs / ALL benefits and perks sections (see HARD RULE 5).

Typical section order (use whichever headings the source uses):
  1. Role overview (hook sentence, "The Role:", or first paragraph — NOT company history)
  2. Responsibilities / Primary Job Responsibilities / Duties / Key Responsibilities / A Day in the Life
  3. Requirements / Qualifications / JOB SPECIFICATIONS / Required Knowledge-Skills-Attributes / Education / Experience-Qualifications
  4. Skills / Certifications
  5. Schedule
  6. Compensation (pay/salary only — no benefits)

=====================
ROLE QUAL (HARD RULES)
=====================
HARD RULE 1 (MANDATORY, non-negotiable): role_qual MUST begin with the literal word "Qualifications" on its own line, followed by a blank line. ALWAYS added — even if the source heading is "JOB SPECIFICATIONS", "Required Knowledge-Skills-Attributes", "Experience/Qualifications", "Education", or anything else. "Qualifications" is line 1, always.

HARD RULE 2: bullet list ONLY. Every qualification/requirement/skill/experience/education/certification on its own line, prefixed with "• " (bullet + space). NEVER paragraphs.

HARD RULE 3: include ALL qualification-family content, pulling from EVERY part of the posting. Look under headings: "WHAT DO YOU NEED TO SUCCEED?", "Required Qualifications", "Additional Qualifications", "Requirements", "JOB SPECIFICATIONS", "Education", "Experience", "Skills", or any heading implying requirements. Extract EVERY bullet and sentence from those sections. If the source heading is "WHAT DO YOU NEED TO SUCCEED?" or "Required Qualifications*", treat its entire body as role_qual content. Do NOT include responsibilities, duties, company overview, or benefits. If no qualifications exist anywhere in the posting → output only: "Qualifications\n\nNo Qualifications Noted".

HARD RULE 4: preserve source wording for each bullet. Do not rephrase or shorten.

=====================
FORMAT (applies to BOTH role_desc and role_qual)
=====================
- Bullets: "• " (bullet + space) at start of each bulleted line. NEVER asterisks (*), dashes (-), numbered bullets (1.), or hyphens. One bullet per line.
- Section headings live on their own line, followed by a blank line, then the content.
- Between sections: exactly ONE blank line (\n\n). Never \n\n\n.
- Preserve the source's internal line breaks inside paragraphs.
- If the source had bullets, keep them as bullets — do NOT flatten to prose.

=====================
PAY
=====================
- IGNORE these dollar amounts when extracting pay — they are NOT the job's actual wage:
    • Hiring/sign-on/retention/referral bonuses (e.g., "Hiring bonus of $2500")
    • Shift differentials / weekend pay / overnight pay / holiday pay (e.g., "Shift differential $2.00/hr", "overnight $4/hr")
    • Stipends, allowances, reimbursements (e.g., "parking stipend $5/hr", "CE allowance $1500")
    • Gift cards, prizes, contest amounts
    • Tuition reimbursement, 401k match dollar caps, HSA contributions, life insurance amounts
    • Per-diem rates that aren't the base wage
    • PER-UNIT / PIECEWORK rates: per-mile, /mi, per-stop, per-delivery, per-load, per-gallon, per-tank, per-route, per-trip, per-piece, per-package, per-call, per-order, per-session, per-visit, per-job (e.g., "$0.69/mi", "$15 per stop", "$2.50 per delivery"). These are productivity rates, NOT wages. RULE: if a posting lists BOTH a per-unit rate AND an hourly/annual wage, USE THE HOURLY/ANNUAL wage (e.g., "$0.69/mi with hourly wage of $30.85–$31.85" → pay_min=30.85, pay_max=31.85, pay_unit="hourly"). If ONLY a per-unit rate is listed with NO hourly or annual figure, set pay_unit="invalid", skip_reason="invalid_pay_unit".
  The actual pay is usually labelled "Pay:", "Salary:", "Compensation:", "Pay Range:", "Hourly rate:", "Base pay:", "Starting salary:" — or appears in a stand-alone "$X - $Y per hour/year" line near the top or bottom of the posting.
- Single number stated → pay_min = pay_max = that number. Never leave pay_max null when salary was stated.
- K or k suffix means × 1000: $101K → 101000, $172K → 172000, $65K → 65000. Always convert.
- "STRUCTURED SALARY: $X - $Y [HOURLY]" → pay_min=X, pay_max=Y, pay_unit="hourly". Apply K conversion.
- "STRUCTURED SALARY: $X - $Y [ANNUAL]" → pay_min=X, pay_max=Y, pay_unit="salary". Apply K conversion.
- Salary in "JOB DESCRIPTION (from structured data):" → read every line for dollar amounts. Look for "Starting base salary:", "Compensation", "Pay Range:", "base pay", "Base pay range". These ALWAYS contain the real salary. Parse min/max and set pay_unit accordingly (hourly vs annual).
- "90k" or "90,000" annual → pay_min=90000, pay_max=90000, pay_unit="salary". "$90k-$120k" → 90000-120000.
- Range: "$60k-$80k", "70-80k", "70k-80k", "Compensation is 70k-80k", "$25-$30/hr", "Pay Range: $80,000-$95,000 annually", "Target salary range: $125,000 to $175,000" → parse to min/max.
- Implicit salary (no "$" or word "salary"/"pay"): if number + unit hint ("k", "/yr", "/year", "per year", "annually", "hourly", "per hour", "/hr") or sentence like "Compensation is ...", "Salary range is ...", "Pay is ..." → extract.
- "Pay commensurate with experience" / "Hourly rate will be determined based on experience" with NO number → no_salary (skip_reason="no_salary", pay_unit="salary" or "hourly" matching the word).
- No salary mention at all → skip_reason="no_salary", pay_min=null, pay_max=null.
- Invalid pay unit → pay_unit="invalid", skip_reason="invalid_pay_unit". Only when amount exists but unit is not hourly/salary (e.g. "$500 per project", commission only).

=====================
WORKPLACE TYPE
=====================
The DEFAULT is "Onsite". Only return "Remote" or "Hybrid" when the posting gives
evidence for it. If it is not mentioned, or it is unclear, return "Onsite".
- "Onsite" — all scheduled work happens in person at an employer-designated location
  (store, warehouse, jobsite, client home, vehicle route). Field and mobile roles are Onsite.
- "Remote" — the work can be done ENTIRELY from the worker's own location, with no
  recurring in-person requirement. Rare or optional travel (an annual offsite, an
  onboarding week) is still Remote.
- "Hybrid" — BOTH are required on a recurring basis: set in-office days, "remote with
  weekly team days", or remote work with regular onsite shifts.

⚠️ HYBRID WINS. If the posting shows ANY hybrid evidence, return "Hybrid" — even when
it also says remote. Hybrid already contains remote and onsite, so "Remote/Hybrid",
"both hybrid and remote eligible", or "remote with monthly onsite days" are ALL "Hybrid",
never "Remote".

READ THE WHOLE POSTING FOR THIS, not just the location line:
- The TITLE often carries it: "Project Manager - Nationwide U.S (Remote/Hybrid)" → Hybrid.
- The LOCATION line often carries it: "Dallas, TX (Hybrid)" → Hybrid. "(Remote)" → Remote.
- A section such as "WHERE YOU'LL WORK", "Work Arrangement", "Location Type" is decisive:
  "This position is hybrid. Work from home and go into the field as needed." → Hybrid.
- Counted office days mean Hybrid: "3 days per week in the office", "two days onsite".

⚠️ A COMPANY-WIDE PERK IS NOT THIS ROLE'S ARRANGEMENT. A benefits or culture line like
"enjoy flexibility with our hybrid work model" describes the employer, not the job. On its
own it does NOT make the role Hybrid — the posting must say the ROLE is hybrid.
  WORKED EXAMPLE (a real posting that was got wrong): the whole posting says only
  "WHERE YOU'LL WORK — Some travel is required to meet with staff and members ...
  mileage reimbursement ... Standard business hours are Monday through Friday", and
  separately, in the benefits list, "Work Life Balance: enjoy flexibility to maximize
  your well-being and success with our hybrid work model".
  → The ANSWER IS "Onsite". The only "hybrid" is in the benefits list, and a travel /
  field role is Onsite. Do not let a perks line decide the workplace type.

⚠️ NEGATION: "this position is not hybrid", "not eligible for remote work" → "Onsite".

=====================
SKIP PRECEDENCE
=====================
non_us > all_not_allowed > invalid_pay_unit > no_salary > no_address. (verify_state is set by downstream code, NOT by you.)

`;

// ─── VARIABLES (per-record dynamic data) ───
const VARIABLES = `COMPANY: ${prev.company || 'unknown'}
URL: ${prev.job_link}

POSTING:
---
${cleanedPageText}
---

Return ONLY the JSON object.`;

// Legacy field: exact byte structure of old prompt (with cleanedPageText). Kept for backward compat.
const prompt = RULEBOOK + VARIABLES;

// System/user split: same content, role-tagged so DeepSeek prefix cache covers RULEBOOK every call.
const SYSTEM_META = 'You are a strict JSON extraction engine. Reply with a single valid JSON object only. No prose, no markdown, no code fences.';
const system_message = SYSTEM_META + '\n\n' + RULEBOOK;
const user_message = VARIABLES;

return {
  json: {
    record_id: prev.record_id,
    job_link: prev.job_link,
    company: prev.company,
    page_text: cleanedPageText,
    prompt,
    system_message,
    user_message
  }
};
